messages:
maria: escalated from support — AcmeApp reporting sudden p95/p99 regression after we onboarded new-model-3 + tokenizer v2.1. They see p99 ~9.8s for long-context queries (>=24k). p95 also up. Started ~2025-12-09 14:10 UTC. Customer very impacted.

sam: thanks — can you paste minimal repro and any request/response headers they sent?

maria: pasted what they sent (redacted):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, X-Model: new-model-3, X-Context-Len: 32768
Body: {"prompt": "<24k tokens of system+user>"}
```
They included timing from their client: median ~350ms, p95 ~1.2s, p99 jumped from 2.8s -> 9.8s after our change.

liam: I looked at runtime traces for that org — saw a sharp increase in `kv-cache-miss` events around the same time. Also noticed many requests are falling back to slower attention path (fallback_kernel) when tokenized length spikes.

anya: tokenizer v2.1 changed how some special sequences split (more subtoken fragmentation for long prompts). Two effects: 1) token count increases ~8-12% on some prompts; 2) leading context distribution changes which reduces effective prefix reuse for KV caching.

sam: that matches: higher token count -> larger KV sizes -> more memory pressure -> more cache evictions -> more recompute -> high p99. Any immediate mitigations?

maria: customer can't move away from long prompts. They asked for a hotfix.

liam: short-term options:
- route AcmeApp traffic to `new-model-3-legacy-tokenizer` variant (pin model variant)
- enable prefix-level sticky caching for that org (reduce eviction)
- temporary rollback of tokenizer v2.1 on that shard

maria: customer prefers routing to legacy variant while you patch tokenizer. Will that be low-risk?

liam: yes — I can add a route rule in the edge router to split 100% to legacy variant for their org id. Takes 5-10m. Low-risk.

deploy-bot: scheduled deployment: route-update for org=acmeapp -> new-model-3-legacy-tokenizer at 2025-12-09T14:55Z. CI checks passed.

ops-bot: INC-2025-8421 created (latency spike, new-model-3). Pager duty notified.

sam: while routing, please collect detailed traces (kv-cache-hit/miss, kernel-choice, token_count, kernel_time). I'll instrument a temporary metric `tokenizer.delta_tokenpct` to track percentage change vs baseline.

maria: rolling routing now per request — confirmed: after traffic moved, AcmeApp reports p99 dropped to 3.2s within 15 minutes. They reported no functional change.

anya: thanks. I'll open a PR to: 1) revert the fragmentation rule that caused extra subtokens, 2) add regression tests with 16k/32k prompts, and 3) add an end-to-end perf test that runs on the onboarding harness.

liam: longer-term runtime mitigations we should do:
- token-count-aware kernel selection early at ingress (fast path before tokenizer completes)
- smarter KV retention heuristics that weight by likely reuse (prefix-frequency)
- per-org prefetched prefix caches for heavy long-context customers

sam: please also add an alert for `kv-cache-miss_rate > 0.3 AND p99_lat > baseline*2` so we catch this class earlier.

maria: shared the rollback routing details and customer confirmation in the ticket. Customer asked about billing — they saw more tokens billed because tokenization increased. I told them we'll credit spike window once patch done.

anya: note for the patch: tokenizer change was intended to fix edge-case with #anon tokens. We need to preserve that fix without increasing subtoken count for long sequences. I'll iterate and include deterministic token-count checks in the tokenizer CI.

liam: created short repro harness that runs the customer's prompt set across both tokenizers and runtime kernels. Results attached in ticket (internal link): https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-8421/traces

sam: next steps (owner tags):
- maria: own customer comms + confirm credits (status: in progress)
- liam: implement routing & collect traces (done)
- anya: tokenizer patch + tests (WIP)
- sam: alerts & kernel heuristics spec (todo)

maria: customer is satisfied with routing and temporary credit offer. They asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll tell them ~48-72h pending PR + QA.

liam: note — also saw a few other low-volume orgs with similar patterns; I'll proactively route any org with >20 long-context failures to legacy tokenizer until patch ships.

anya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/tokenizer/pulls/452 — adds regression tests and toggles the special-sequence rule. Requesting review from runtime and qa.

sam: thanks everyone. Once patch passes, plan: 1) staged rollout 2) monitor kv-cache-miss + p99 3) enable default optimizer. :thumbsup:

maria: closing loop with customer now, leaving thread for followups.

liam: leaving postmortem notes in INC ticket with root cause: tokenizer-induced token-count inflation -> KV cache pressure -> fallback kernel -> p99 spike. Suggested long-term: token-aware routing and per-org prefix caches.

deploy-bot: deployment log: route-update rolled back to default for org=acmeapp at 2025-12-11T10:12Z (after staged patch verified).

ops-bot: incident INC-2025-8421 resolved (summary: tokenizer patch + routing + credits).
